module_title: Advanced Analysis - Constitutional Amendments, GST Council, and ITC
introduction: This advanced level focuses on the specific Constitutional Amendments that made GST legally possible. We will also understand the voting power structure of the GST Council and the critical mechanism of 'Input Tax Credit' (ITC).

core_concepts.title: Constitutional Amendment
core_concepts.description:
Since the taxation powers of both the Center and States had to be altered, a Constitutional Amendment was mandatory. 
- 122nd Constitutional Amendment Bill: Introduced in Parliament. 
- 101st Constitutional Amendment Act (2016): Passed and signed by the President, becoming the 101st law.

core_concepts.title: The GST Council (Article 279A)
core_concepts.description:
All decisions regarding GST (like changing tax rates) are taken by the 'GST Council'. 
- Chairperson: Union Finance Minister. 
- Members: Finance Ministers of all States. 
It is considered the finest example of 'Cooperative Federalism' in India.

core_concepts.title: Voting Power in the GST Council
core_concepts.description:
This is highly complex and critical. Every decision in the Council must be passed by a '75% majority' (3/4th majority). 
- The Central Government holds a weightage of '1/3rd' of the total votes. 
- All State Governments combined hold a weightage of '2/3rd' of the total votes. 
(Meaning neither the Center nor the States can pass a decision alone).

core_concepts.title: Input Tax Credit (ITC)
core_concepts.description: This is the soul of GST. When a manufacturer buys raw materials, they pay GST on them. Later, when they sell the final product, they can deduct the GST they already paid from their final GST liability. This mechanism is called ITC, and it prevents the cascading effect.

important_entities.name: New Constitutional Articles Added
important_entities.significance:
1. Article 246A: Gives special power to Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on GST. 
2. Article 269A: Rules for Inter-State trade (IGST). 
3. Article 279A: Formation of the GST Council.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: This is the biggest trap in UPSC and State PCS. If the question asks 'Which Amendment BILL was GST?', the answer is 122nd. If it asks 'Which Amendment ACT was GST?', the answer is 101st.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Center = 1/3 vote. States = 2/3 vote. Passing Marks = 75%.

exam_strategy_tips: Mandatorily memorize Article 279A (GST Council). It has been directly asked in multiple recent competitive exams.
